title: A New and Complete Illustration of the Celestial Science of Astrology
author: Ebenezer Sibly
description: A New and Complete Illustration of the Celestial Science of Astrology, or the Art of Foretelling Future Events and Contingencies by the Aspects, Positions and Influences of the Heavenly Bodies, by Ebenezer Sibly (1751-c. 1799), the English physician, astrologer and Freemason (first published in parts from 1784 and reissued many times). Its title page describes it as 'founded on natural philosophy, scripture, reason and the mathematics', demonstrating 'the abstruse doctrine of the stars, of magic, divination, exorcism and familiarity with spirits', the calculation of nativities and horary questions, drawn from the writings of over five hundred authors. Its four parts cover astrological principles and the planets, signs and houses, the calculation and judgement of nativities, horary astrology, and the occult sciences of magic, spirits and witchcraft. It contains the famous horoscope of the United States (the 'Sibly chart' for 4 July 1776) and many engraved plates. It was hugely influential in reviving English astrology.
